title: Standard RFID Wood Card — FSC-Certified Body
summary: The Standard RFID Wood Card is an FSC-certified maple, bamboo, or beech card with a laminated RFID/NFC inlay and a 2–5 cm typical read range. It is the entry point for hospitality, membership, and luxury-branding programs that want a biodegradable card without giving up read range or chip choice. Available with NTAG 213/215/216, NTAG 424 DNA, MIFARE Classic 1k, MIFARE Plus EV2, MIFARE DESFire EV2/EV3, or ICODE SLIX inlays; MOQ is 500 pieces.

sections.title: Who the standard wood card is for
sections.intro: Most key cards are a small piece of PVC that will outlive the hotel that issued them. The Standard RFID Wood Card is the fix for programs that would rather not laminate that thought into the welcome kit: same chips, same locks, same encoding as a plastic card, with a body your sustainability report can actually cite. It is the workhorse SKU of our wood family — stocked species, standard CR80 footprint, encoding included. Still weighing materials? Start with the [hotel key card material selection guide](/guides/hotel-key-card-material-selection/) or the head-to-head [PVC vs wood vs PLA comparison](/compare/pvc-vs-wood-vs-pla-hotel-key-cards/).

sections.title: The FSC part — sustainability that survives an audit
sections.intro: A sustainability claim without paperwork is interior decorating. FSC chain-of-custody certification is the paperwork: a third-party-audited trail from managed forest to card factory, document by document. If the program's story leans on renewal speed instead, the [bamboo card](/products/rfid-cards/rfid-bamboo-card/) regrows its raw material in years rather than decades; for grain-forward premium builds, the [hardwood veneer card](/products/rfid-cards/rfid-wooden-card/) is the flagship.

image.alt: Five-step chain-of-custody flow for the standard RFID wood card: FSC-certified forest, veneer mill with chain-of-custody paper trail, card factory where the inlay is embedded and engraved, 18–24 months in service as a hotel or membership card, then an end-of-life fork — the wood body biodegrades while the RFID inlay is routed to e-waste recycling.

checklist: FSC chain-of-custody documentation for the wood stock ships with your order — file it with the program's sustainability records.
Verify any FSC claim (ours included) against the FSC public certificate search before you buy.
EU buyers: wood products placed on the EU market fall under Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 (EUDR) due diligence — CoC records feed that statement.
End of life is a split, not a slogan: the wood body biodegrades; the inlay (chip + antenna) goes through standard e-waste channels, and we can supply the BOM for downstream processing.

sections.title: Wood vs PVC — the honest trade
sections.intro: PVC wins most spec-sheet arguments; wood wins the moment the guest picks the card up. Buying wood well means knowing exactly which argument you are in — and what each material does after checkout.

sections.title: Where wood says no
sections.intro: Wood declines a few briefs, and it is cheaper to hear the no before the pilot order than after it. The pattern to remember: standing water, autoclaves, and any job where the card is disposable by design.
bullets: One-time event passes: at disposable volumes the per-piece economics belong to PVC or paper — wood is a keeper, not a throwaway.
Wet environments: humidity and standing water can warp or stain the wood. Specify the sealed lacquer finish, and keep it off pool-deck duty.
Edge-to-edge color: grain shows through artwork. Smooth full-bleed color needs UV printing or a veneer overlay — or, honestly, a PVC card.
Industrial laundry and autoclave cycles: wood does not survive them. That job belongs to PPS or silicone tags.

sections.title: Applications — where the wood card earns its keep
sections.intro: The standard wood card slots into any 13.56 MHz workflow a PVC card already serves, so the question is where the material premium pays back. Four places, reliably. For lock-side planning start at the [hotel key cards solution](/solutions/hotel-key-cards/); if door hardware favors a fob, the [wooden keyfob](/products/rfid-keyfobs/rfid-wooden-keyfob/) carries the same story on a keyring.

sections.title: Personalization and encoding
sections.intro: Wood personalization happens at the factory, not at the front desk — laser engraving is permanent by design, and desktop card printers decline wood politely. Encoding is unaffected: the chips are written exactly as they would be in a PVC body. For full-color artwork pipelines see the [custom-printed NFC card](/products/rfid-cards/nfc-card-custom-printing/); for lock-data workflows, the [hotel key card encoding guide](/guides/hotel-key-card-encoding/).
bullets: Laser engraving (recommended for wood): permanent dark-on-grain logos, text, QR codes, and sequential numbering — no ink, no lamination step.
UV printing: full-color artwork directly on the wood face when the brand needs more than monochrome.
Hot-stamp foil and embossed numbering on request for premium tiers.
Encoding included: UID lock, NDEF records, and custom data blocks are written before shipping at no extra unit cost.

sections.title: How we test before shipping
sections.intro: Wood is a natural material; the QC pass is what keeps natural from drifting into variable. Every wood card clears the same functional gate as our PVC cards, plus a dimensional check the plastic never needs.
checklist: 100% functional read test on every encoded card.
Dimensional check: thickness within ±0.05 mm, flatness within 0.2 mm.
24-hour lamination cure rest before engraving or shipping.
Engraving QC: laser depth, contrast, and registration checked visually.
Pack-out in individual sleeves or a branded box on request.

faq.question: Can the wood card be used in hotel locks?
faq.answer: Yes, with the right chip family. MIFARE Plus EV2 and MIFARE DESFire EV3 wood cards work with Saflok, VingCard, Onity, Salto, and Häfele Dialock locks. Confirm the lock model and firmware version when ordering so we match the chip-family expectation.

faq.question: How long does the wood card last in daily hospitality use?
faq.answer: Expect 18–24 months of typical hotel-room use before mechanical wear becomes visible. Lamination is sealed and the chip is unaffected, but the wood surface eventually shows scratching from key chains and pockets. PVC lasts 36–48 months in the same use.

faq.question: Can I get a custom wood species?
faq.answer: Maple, bamboo, and beech are stocked. Walnut, cherry, and oak are available on request with longer lead times and a small species premium. We will share dimensional samples before committing to a production run.

faq.question: Is the wood card recyclable?
faq.answer: The wood body is biodegradable. The chip and antenna are recyclable through standard e-waste channels. We do not yet offer a take-back program; if your sustainability audit needs end-of-life documentation, we can supply the chip and antenna BOM for downstream processing.

faq.question: Can wood cards run through our existing card printers?
faq.answer: No. Wood cards do not feed through desktop thermal-retransfer or direct-to-card printers; personalization (laser engraving or UV printing) is done at the factory before shipping. Encoding is unaffected — front-desk and lock-system encoders write the chip exactly as they write a PVC card, because the chip families are identical.

faq.question: What are the MOQ and lead times for the standard wood card?
faq.answer: MOQ is 500 pieces per chip family and finish combination. Samples take 7–10 working days because the wood lamination needs a full cure before engraving, and reorders ship in 12–18 working days. Encoding (UID lock, NDEF, custom blocks) is included in the unit price.

faq.question: Is the wood FSC-certified, and what documentation comes with an order?
faq.answer: Yes. The stocked maple, bamboo, and beech bodies come from FSC chain-of-custody certified supply, and chain-of-custody documentation ships with the order. For EU buyers, that documentation supports the due-diligence statement required for wood products under the EU Deforestation Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2023/1115.

faq.question: Does the wood body change the read range compared with PVC?
faq.answer: Slightly. A standard wood card reads at 2–5 cm on typical HF readers — the same band as PVC — and up to 7 cm with MIFARE Plus EV2 on a high-power reader. Wood's moisture content shifts antenna tuning a little more than PVC laminate does, which is why every card passes a 100% read test before shipping.
